definition: A measure of the quantity of matter in an object, in kilograms (kg); it changes only if matter is added or removed, not when the object is moved to another place.
The gravitational force on an object because it has mass, in newtons (N); it acts towards the centre of the Earth (or other body) and is not the same as mass.
The gravitational force per unit mass, $g = \frac{W}{m}$, in N/kg; it equals the acceleration of free fall, about $9.8\ \text{N/kg}$ near the Earth's surface.
